findings.title: Split reviews retain only the first part’s spend
findings.description: Each part receives usage metadata, but `fold_review_parts()` copies only the first part’s metadata. Subsequent parts’ tokens, turns, duration, and cost disappear from run statistics. A direct reproduction confirmed this. Aggregate every part’s usage before returning the folded result.

findings.title: Failed split-review parts violate the folding contract
findings.description: The new failure return has empty outputs, while `fold_review_parts()` requires every part to identify its input file. With multiple parts, a provider failure therefore triggers a secondary `TypeError`; the outer handler discards the captured usage. This was reproduced directly. Preserve the part identity and failure status through folding.

findings.title: Loop and fan-out spend never reaches run statistics
findings.description: The report sums only persisted top-level action results. However, loop execution keeps earlier iterations in `StepResult.prior_rounds`, which `StateManager._append_step()` does not serialize. Fan-out reducers likewise discard branch usage metadata. Consequently, loops report only their final iteration and fan-outs omit their branch spend. Persist these records and include them exactly once in totals; add end-to-end coverage for both structures.

findings.title: Failed compaction drops available usage telemetry
findings.description: The exception branch returns without stamping usage, even when the SDK raises a `ProviderError` carrying completed-turn telemetry. Failed compactions therefore lose known spend, unlike dispatch and summary failures. Capture the exception’s telemetry and test that it survives the returned failure result.
